output.title: Synthetic test data: use it for the decision, not the demo
output.body:
Synthetic test data is useful when it helps you make a bounded workflow decision faster. It is less useful when it turns into a project of its own.

For a small business, the question is simple: are you using synthetic data because you need privacy, scale, or a safe way to show the control logic — or because no one has tried the real workflow yet?

If the pilot is a repeatable task like invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, start smaller. Use a limited real-data subset, clear rules, and a human approval step where money or another high-risk decision is involved. That keeps the work focused on the actual workflow instead of on perfect fake data.

Bareni’s accounts-payable demo is a good boundary example. It uses entirely synthetic data to show the mechanics: text-based extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But it also has limits: the default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF/scan ingestion and OCR are not implemented. So it is useful for showing control logic, not for pretending it is ready for every real invoice pile.

My practical next step: pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of real records. Then ask whether synthetic data is solving a real testing problem, or just delaying the moment you learn what the workflow actually needs. If the answer is the second one, the spreadsheet has already won.
